meta.title:
HTV Silicone Rubber Insulator Simulation
PhD Thesis

summary: This research project focuses on simulating electric field distribution in HTV silicone rubber polymer insulators under varying contamination and voltage conditions. Using advanced FEM analysis, it helps predict high-risk failure zones and improves understanding of insulation behavior in real-world environments.

challenge.description: Polymer insulators operating in polluted and wet environments are highly prone to electrical tracking, surface erosion, and premature failure. Traditional testing methods are expensive, time-consuming, and require extensive physical prototyping, making material evaluation inefficient. Additionally, unpredictable voltage distribution across contaminated surfaces creates uncertainty in performance prediction and lifespan estimation.

methodology.title: Model Development
methodology.description: Created detailed 3D models of polymer insulators and defined material properties including HTV silicone rubber characteristics and contamination layers.

methodology.title: FEM Simulation & Contamination Analysis
methodology.description: Performed ANSYS-based electric field simulations under varying contamination conditions such as pollutant layers, water droplets, and tracking paths across voltage ranges from 2.5 kV to 6 kV.

methodology.title: Performance Evaluation & Optimization
methodology.description: Analyzed electric field distribution results to identify high-risk breakdown zones and recommended design improvements for better hydrophobicity and voltage distribution control.

impact.label: Physical Testing Dependency
impact.description: Minimized reliance on costly and time-consuming physical prototype testing through accurate simulation-based evaluation.

impact.label: Failure Prediction Accuracy
impact.description: Enabled better identification of high-risk tracking and erosion zones using FEM-based electric field analysis.

impact.label: Material Selection Insight
impact.description: Validated HTV silicone rubber as a high-performance insulating material with improved resistance to contamination and erosion.
